assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into programmable adaptors that recruit E3 ligases to chosen proteins, opening a drug modality that inhibitors cannot reach. It is a clear molecular-design principle with direct clinical consequences, which is the kind of discovery that changes what chemists and clinicians can do.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made major later advances, so a three-person split is contestable.
assessment.maturity: PROTACs are in multiple clinical trials and the mechanism is reproduced widely. Approval of a degrader drug is still pending as far as I know, which could make recognition slightly early, but the chemistry is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be framed as PROTACs, molecular glues, or both, and who anchors each part.
I cannot verify the current state of late-stage clinical results from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry behind siRNA and mRNA medicines, including the COVID-19 vaccines. Their lipid design principles control encapsulation, endosomal escape and tolerability. The societal impact is very large and demonstrable, and the design rules are chemical.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group of Cullis, Hope and Madden established ionizable lipid formulation, and MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer added key lipid and delivery advances. The credit is spread across many people and companies, so a clean trio is difficult. Cullis seems most central, with Anderson and Langer as plausible partners.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale, with several approved products. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized mRNA modification, which leaves the delivery chemistry open for a Chemistry prize.
uncertainties: Allocation among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is disputed and patent-entangled.
Overlap with the earlier Medicine recognition could be seen as duplication.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis, based on reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule detection, reduced the cost of DNA reading by orders of magnitude and underlies modern genomics and diagnostics. It is chemistry-driven and has had a huge effect on biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the Solexa approach and its chemistry, which gives a compact two-person prize. Rothberg, Ju, Mayer and others contributed alternative platforms, so competing claims exist.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of use across medicine, microbiology and biology. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Credit relative to the 454 pyrosequencing, Ju and Mayer contributions is not fully settled.
Whether the Committee views sequencing as a chemistry or a biology advance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs, so protein chemistry can be programmed in living systems. It is original, conceptually clean and broadly used in biophysics, chemical biology and protein therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal pair strategy in E. coli and eukaryotes, and Chin extended it to multiple codons, mutually orthogonal systems and genome recoding. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed decisive demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and reproduced. Some applications such as synthetic organisms are still developing, but the core method is stable.
uncertainties: Which of Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama deserve recognition alongside Schultz and Chin is unresolved.
Overlap with the 2018 directed evolution prize is modest but may be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts chemistry on DNA bases into a precise genome-editing tool without double-strand breaks, and is already in clinical use. It is a good example of molecular design leading to a therapeutic platform, and it builds on the 2020 CRISPR prize.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the decisive invention with Komor and Gaudelli as lead co-inventors. Nishida and Kondo made an independent cytidine-deaminase variant, so a single-person prize is plausible but could attract credit questions.
assessment.maturity: First clinical results are appearing, and the method is adopted worldwide. Timing may be somewhat early for the longest-term clinical outcomes.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers to pair base and prime editing as one Liu prize.
Long-term safety and efficacy data are incomplete as far as I know.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed how cells organize biochemistry without membranes, linking sequence-encoded weak multivalent interactions to function. It resonates with my own work on peptide folding and assembly and has changed how disease mechanisms are studied.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed liquid-like P granules, and Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction physical chemistry. Pappu and Mittag also made major quantitative contributions, so the credit is broad.
assessment.maturity: The concept is influential but controversial in places, as the physiological relevance of some condensates is still debated and methodological artifacts have been identified. Probably somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Ongoing debate over the physiological reality of specific condensates.
Allocation between cell-biology and physical-chemistry contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins, giving precise control over modifications and unnatural residues. It has been a central method in chemical biology and underlies many protein-engineering strategies.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported the original native chemical ligation, and Muir developed expressed protein ligation for semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu extended the methods, so the credit is spread.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with decades of use. The late recognition is not a concern, but newer biological tools may have reduced its current profile.
uncertainties: Whether the field would view the prize as synthesis or semisynthesis centered.
Priority claims relating to related ligation chemistries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to read the functional state of enzymes directly in complex proteomes and supports covalent ligand discovery. It is a widely used chemical-proteomic platform, and it is very relevant to bioanalytical chemistry and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the clear leader of the method and its application to the proteome. Bogyo and Overkleeft made strong probe design contributions, and Weerapana contributed to cysteine reactivity profiling.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly adopted in academia and industry. The influence on approved drugs is still indirect.
uncertainties: Whether a two-person or single-person prize best represents the field.
Industrial impact is harder to measure from my own knowledge.
